skill.name: azure-upgrade
skill.description: Assess Azure upgrade readiness, migrate Linux Functions to Flex Consumption, modernize Azure Java SDKs, and route Redis migrations to dedicated skills.
skill.summary: Guides safe Azure service upgrades and Java SDK modernization with assessment, automation, and validation steps.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation-only false positives, especially PowerShell mentions, Markdown links, and inline code formatting. Confirmed risks remain in executable migration helpers and Azure CLI guidance, including build-tool execution, project file mutation, network fetches, sensitive configuration exposure, and overbroad autonomous workflow language.

remediation.issue: Overbroad no-pause and no-stop workflow language
remediation.suggestion: State that host rules, user instructions, safety limits, and explicit confirmations always take priority over migration completion goals.

remediation.issue: Fixed rewrite.yml path can overwrite or delete user configuration
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique temporary file, detect existing rewrite.yml, and restore or preserve any user-owned file during cleanup.

remediation.issue: Function App settings and storage connection strings are printed or handled in shell variables
remediation.suggestion: Redact app setting values, avoid echoing secrets, prefer managed identity, and document secure handling for temporary credentials.

remediation.issue: Unquoted shell variables in deployment package handling
remediation.suggestion: Quote variables, validate package names, reject path separators, and write downloads to a controlled temporary directory.

remediation.issue: Maven, Gradle, OpenRewrite, and Azure CLI commands can execute code or change resources
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, show dry-run plans when possible, and warn that project build scripts may execute code.

remediation.issue: Remote BOM metadata controls dependency rewrite decisions
remediation.suggestion: Document the trusted source, support offline review, and consider checksum or signed-source verification where available.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Agent Autonomy Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The Java workflow tells the agent to avoid pausing, treats token and time limits as invalid, and proceeds directly to execution. These instructions can conflict with host limits, user confirmation, and safe scope control.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited text directly imposes no-pause and no-stop behavior. It does not claim system authority, but it can override user or host boundaries.

semantic_findings.title: Project Configuration Overwrite and Deletion Risk
semantic_findings.description: The BOM helper writes rewrite.yml in the project root and later removes that path. A preexisting OpenRewrite configuration can be overwritten or deleted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code constructs a fixed rewrite.yml path, writes it, and removes it during cleanup. There is no check, backup, or restore for an existing user file.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Azure Configuration Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The automation guidance collects and prints app settings, then reads the AzureWebJobsStorage connection string for storage access. These values commonly contain secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands explicitly collect app settings and a storage connection string. Azure app settings commonly include credentials and tokens.

semantic_findings.title: Unquoted Deployment Package Filename
semantic_findings.description: The package name returned from blob storage is used unquoted as the local output file path. Blob names with spaces, option-like prefixes, or path separators can cause unintended behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The package name comes from remote blob metadata and is expanded unquoted in a shell command. This creates plausible parsing and file path risks.

content.user_title: Upgrade Azure Functions and Java SDKs
content.value_statement: Azure upgrades can expose hidden compatibility, identity, and rollback risks. This skill provides structured assessment, migration guidance, and validation steps for supported Azure upgrade paths.
actual_capabilities: Assesses Azure Functions Consumption to Flex Consumption readiness.
Guides Azure CLI migration, deployment, validation, and rollback planning.
Modernizes Java projects from legacy com.microsoft.azure packages to com.azure packages.
Uses an included Python helper to resolve and apply the latest Azure SDK BOM.

best_practices: Generate an assessment and rollback plan before running upgrade commands.
Prefer managed identity and identity-based configuration over connection strings or stored keys.
Validate the new resource completely before deleting or disabling the original resource.
anti_patterns: Running migration commands before confirming the target subscription, region, and resource names.
Printing full app settings, connection strings, or deployment package details into logs.
Treating a partial Java SDK migration or failing test suite as acceptable completion.

faq.question: Can this skill upgrade Windows Function Apps to Flex Consumption?
faq.answer: No. The included Flex Consumption path is for Linux Function Apps only.

faq.question: Does it delete the original Function App?
faq.answer: No. Destructive cleanup requires explicit user confirmation after validation.

faq.question: Can it migrate Azure Cache for Redis directly?
faq.answer: No. It identifies the Redis source type and routes users to the correct AMR migration skill.

faq.question: Does the Java flow support non-Java Azure SDK migrations?
faq.answer: No. The Java modernization guidance targets Maven or Gradle projects using legacy Azure Java SDKs.

faq.question: What tools are needed for automation?
faq.answer: Typical runs need Azure CLI, jq, Python, Maven or Gradle, and suitable Azure permissions.

faq.question: Is it safe to run without review?
faq.answer: No. Review generated commands, redacted settings, project file changes, and resource changes before execution.
